chunks: From him, from his father, from Haroun ibn al-Jahm, from Hafs ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who fears retaliation should refrain from oppressing the people.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title for Imam Ali (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الْقِصَاصَ: Retaliation or retribution, often referring to just recompense in this context.

ai.seo_question: What is the connection between fearing retaliation and avoiding oppression in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith establishes a psychological and spiritual mechanism for social justice, where the fear of *qisas* (retribution or retaliation) acts as a deterrent against *zulm* (oppression). In Shia scholarly tradition, this reflects the concept of *taqwa* as a practical safeguard, linking the fear of divine justice with the preservation of human rights in communal life. It underscores that true piety manifests not just in ritual worship but in the restraint from harming others.
